title: Papercap Converse — Deal Notes Refresh (CS/SE handoff)
content:
Context / why this doc exists
- HubSpot record for Papercap Converse was last updated 2026-03-10 and is starting to drift.
- This refresh is meant for CS + SE continuity as the POC moves from “discovery” to active evaluation.

Account snapshot (refresh)
- Company: Papercap Converse (papercap.ai)
- Primary contact: Elena Ruiz (CTO) <elena@papercap.ai>
- Other stakeholder: Jonas Park (Head of Product)
- Segment/tier: SMB (11–50)
- Use cases: in-app chat assistant embedded in customer-facing app; triage + quick answers; support-agent assist + summarization as follow-on.
- Interested products: hosted_api (primary), Optimize (secondary; they care about latency + predictable cost).
- Deployment: public cloud (now); asked about a dedicated/VPC option as a “future” path (not a POC requirement).

What changed since 2026-03-10 (net-new / corrected)
1) Stage + timeline moved
- Stage is now effectively POC / evaluation (not just discovery).
- Forecast close shifted from 2026-04 to 2026-05 based on procurement + security review lead time.
- Target beta launch expectation changed from “6 weeks” to “~8–10 weeks” due to security and analytics instrumentation work.

2) Benchmarks improved (latency)
- Initial engineering trial (early March) showed first-token latency ~280ms under their baseline settings.
- After SE guidance (prefix caching + model variant selection + region pinning), their latest reported p95 first-token is ~190–210ms for US users in staging on scripted prompts.
- Remaining gap: tail latency at higher concurrency; they see sporadic spikes >350ms at ~40 concurrent users (needs more data; possibly client-side reconnect/backpressure behavior).

3) Volume assumptions updated
- Current staging volume: closer to ~8k messages/day (was ~5k/day).
- 6-month target: 30k messages/day (was 25k/day).
- Peak concurrency expectation: 40–55 active users at peak (was 25–40).

4) Security requirements clarified/expanded
- Still required: SOC2, SSO (SAML), audit logging.
- Newly requested: SCIM “nice to have” for later (not a hard blocker for initial launch, but they want a roadmap answer).
- Data residency: still not required.
- They asked for data retention defaults and whether we support configurable retention for logs/requests in the hosted tier.

5) Commercial expectations updated
- ARR estimate nudged upward because volume assumptions increased and they are likely to add Optimize for cost/latency tuning.
- Working estimate range: $12k–$30k ARR (previous HubSpot note: $6k–$18k).
- They want a clearer monthly bill estimate tied to: 30k msgs/day, ~60 tokens/message average, streaming enabled, and a “busy hour” concurrency scenario.

Current blockers / risks (as of 2026-03-22)
- Hosted SLA/SLO clarity: they want something written for uptime (they asked specifically for 99.9%+), and clear language on what is/ isn’t committed for latency.
- Budget confidence: they need a cost model they can defend internally (token cost breakdown + guardrails).
- SSO timeline: SAML is required before production; they asked whether it is available in their tier and how long onboarding takes.
- Tail latency at concurrency: spikes during 40–55 concurrent testing are the main technical risk.

What we told them (latest positioning)
- Streaming: SSE remains the recommended default for their React client; WebSocket is possible but they should only switch if SSE reconnection semantics are limiting.
- Observability: per-request latency + token usage should be included in their internal dashboarding; we can provide logging fields + examples.
- Model strategy: start on Redwood-curated hosted model; keep option to pin a quantized variant later once their prompt shapes stabilize.

POC plan (updated)
- Duration: 3-week POC (was initially 2 weeks).
- Environment: their staging React app with scripted benchmark scenarios.
- Scenarios:
  1) Cold start / first interaction
  2) 10 concurrent
  3) 40 concurrent
  4) NEW: 55 concurrent “busy hour” soak test (30–45 minutes)
- Metrics:
  - p95 first-token latency (goal: <=200ms; acceptable if 200–230ms with documented optimization path)
  - tail latency and reconnect behavior (SSE)
  - error/timeout rate
  - tokens/conversation + cost per 1k tokens

Customer quotes (carried forward)
- Elena Ruiz (CTO): “We need chat to feel instant — if it feels slow customers churn. Can’t accept >200ms for first token ideally.”
- Jonas Park (Head of Product): “If streaming is smooth and predictable cost-wise, we can launch to beta in ~8–10 weeks.”

Next steps (CS/SE action list)
- CS (Nina): send written SLA overview for hosted tier + clarify what is covered vs best-effort for latency.
- SE (Omar): provide updated React SSE streaming example (reconnect/backoff + cancellation) and a short concurrency test harness.
- AE (Marissa): send revised cost estimate table for 30k msgs/day scenario + budget guardrail suggestions.
- Customer: schedule a 45-min security review (SAML, audit logs, retention) and confirm go/no-go criteria for production.

Internal notes to keep HubSpot consistent
- Recommended HubSpot field updates:
  - stage: discovery -> poc/evaluation
  - forecast_close_month: 2026-04 -> 2026-05
  - estimated_arr_range: $6k-$18k -> $12k-$30k
  - blockers: add tail latency at concurrency; add retention/SCIM questions; keep SLA and budgeting
- Owner continuity: AE Marissa Chen; SE Omar Patel; CS point of contact moving forward: Nina Alvarez
